register.name: the Glas function
register.definition: The transparent-medium operation — the lens that does not editorialize what it shows.
register.operation: Takes the Semantic Deviation Principle and its protocol papers as input; returns a narrowed, citationally grounded, externally evaluable statement. It does not amend the founding text.

mantle.note: The register is a function, not a mantle.

editorships._rule: A duovirate is the office, held jointly. A board seat is not the office. The card keeps them apart.

semanticIntegrityMarkers._note: THE ONLY MARKERS WRITTEN AS A PAIR.

markers.gloss: ∮ measures accountable circulation, Ω its inequity — a circulation without its skew is a number without an error bar
the mark invoked as a standard another instrument must meet

surfaceHistory._rule: A surface is a place a reader could find the work. A DEPOSIT IS NOT A SURFACE — it is the archive holding it, which is the opposite. Rows citing deposits were removed.
surfaceHistory._invented: Where no pre-archival surface is recoverable it is RECONSTRUCTED and marked as such, in-universe. An archive that invents a provenance and does not say so is doing the thing it was built against.

rows.note: Inferred from standards, tolerances, a stated instrument and a stated error. An observatory publishes measurements, and measurements have instruments rather than readers.

recordSurfaces._note: The dataset record is the authority; these pages are mirrors and say so.

mainEntity.name: Nobel Glas
mainEntity.disambiguatingDescription: Pessoa-class heteronymic writerly identity in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive; the transparent-medium register, author of the Semantic Deviation Research Program. Not a synonym for the orthonym: the relation is heteronymic and provenance-governed.

_updated._note: The entity object is what a machine fetches instead of parsing the page. It had gone stale against its own card: mantles, editorships and markers were all on the surface and not in the object.
